newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bill proceeds not for budget-ministry.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bill proceeds not for budget-ministry.

text.p: The Russian Finance Ministry does not intend to use proceeds from Wednesday's Treasury bill auction to finance the budget, Bella Zlatkis, head of the ministry's securities and financial markets department, said on Tuesday.

Russian policy is to issue about enough T-bills at regular auctions needed to cover payments on maturing paper, and some traders had said that plans to issue this week twice the required amount indicated budget problems.
Zlatkis told Reuters that one half of the 15 trillion roubles of GKO discount T-bills and OFZ government bonds announced for auction were needed to cover repayments on maturing T-bills.
Remaining bills would be kept and sold, as needed, directly onto the secondary market -- a normal practice, she said.

"The announced volume of paper is not linked to finance ministry wishes to raise additional funds for the budget, but rather to have enough longer paper in our portfolio to regulate demand on the open market," she said.
"Essentially, we will take only half the announced funds and save the rest for later."
The Central Bank must pay 6.3 trillion roubles on maturing six-month bills this Wednesday.
It has said it would issue 10 trillion roubles of eight-month bills and five trillion roubles of an additional tranche of bonds maturing in June 1998 -- both on Wednesday.
